content: The Chronic Care Model (CCM), as endorsed by the American Diabetes Association (ADA), provides a structured approach to managing chronic diseases such as diabetes. It emphasizes six fundamental components: 1. Delivery System Design: This involves creating a proactive and well-coordinated care system that ensures patients receive timely and efficient management of their chronic conditions. 2. Self-Management Support: Patients are empowered with the tools, education, and resources necessary to actively participate in managing their own health and making informed decisions about their care. 3. Decision Support: Clinical decisions are guided by evidence-based guidelines and best practices to ensure that care is both effective and aligned with the latest medical research. 4. Clinical Information Systems: These systems utilize patient registries and other data management tools to track patient outcomes, monitor progress, and facilitate better care coordination. 5. Community Resources: External resources are leveraged to promote healthy lifestyles, providing patients with access to programs and services that support their overall well-being. 6. Health Systems: The focus is on fostering a culture within healthcare organizations that prioritizes quality improvement and patient-centered care.
